newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat given month to replace cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Arafat given month to replace cabinet.

text.p: The Palestinian Legislative Council gave President Yasser Arafat one month on Thursday to dissolve his cabinet and appoint a new one following a corruption probe.
Lawmakers said the 88-member council voted 56-1 to urge Arafat to appoint a new cabinet with "qualified and experienced ministers" by September.

"We hope Arafat will respond to our resolution because the cabinet must be changed. Otherwise, we will study if we should take measures to ensure it be carried out," Speaker of the Council Ahmed Korei told reporters.
The resolution called on the council's auditing committee to ensure it is implemented by Arafat.

In addition to the challenge to clean up his government, Arafat is also under pressure from Israel and the United States to move swiftly against Moslem militants in the wake of a Jerusalem suicide bombing on Wednesday.
The council acted after nine members issued a scathing report this week demanding Arafat curb corruption. The Palestinian president promised to take "all the necessary measures".
The report urged him to sack his entire cabinet and not to reappoint those found to have been corrupt. It recommended at least two ministers suspected of wrongdoing be put on trial.
Minister of Planning Nabil Shaath and Minister of Civilian Affairs Jamil al-Tarifi, accused by the council's panel of corruption and misuse of public funds, denied the allegations.
They defended themselves during a council session on Tuesday and threatened to sue for slander.
The recommendation to fire the cabinet followed increasing complaints by Palestinians and legislators of alleged corruption and mismanagement in the Palestinian Authority.
The report asked Arafat to put on trial and punish those found guilty of corruption in order to restore confidence between the Authority and the people.
Legislators and officials urged Arafat to undertake stringent reforms and not mere cosmetic changes.
An official auditor's report earlier this year found that members of the Palestinian Authority had squandered $326 million in public funds last year.

These findings were the subject of an investigation by a committee appointed by Arafat which reported last week that while money had not been squandered, serious financial, legal and administrative violations had taken place.
The alleged corruption in Palestinian self-rule areas has increased pressure on Arafat from international donors to ensure aid to the ailing Palestinian economy is spent properly.
